prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, in which magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms opened a new regime of precision in time and frequency measurement

statement.case_for: I change my preferred configuration from B051 plus B009 to B051 alone. The case for lattice clocks is the one I can defend most fully. The central step is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, because the magic wavelength lets many neutral atoms be held with the lattice light shift cancelled, and that is what delivered 1e-18 systematic uncertainty and stability. The performance is not a single group's claim: JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, NIST, PTB and SYRTE agree through clock-to-clock comparisons, including intercontinental links, which is the kind of independent confirmation I ask for first. Six of eight members already list it with the same two names, and the consequences (relativistic geodesy, tests of constants and local position invariance, dark-matter searches, the roadmap for the SI second) are measurable rather than promised. I would word the citation around the invention and realization of the lattice clock and the magic-wavelength step, and not around the redefinition of the second, which has not happened.
statement.case_against: The objections to B051 remain real. The lattice clock follows the frequency comb and ion-control prizes, so an outside expert must say explicitly that it is a distinct achievement. The 2001-2003 priority record (Katori, Lemonde and others) and the split of credit between Katori's invention and Ye's accuracy and many-body work still need an archival check, and a Katori-Ye pair leaves out people such as Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley and Bloom. The SI second is not yet redefined, so some of the impact is prospective. Dropping B009 also costs something: IceCube is a real observational discovery of the kind I value, and a single-part clock prize is a narrower statement than the committee may want. I accept that cost over a part whose credit I cannot defend.

responses.point: Kroll would keep B009 off any configuration and not pair it with B051 until the attribution question is answered, because a clock prize has two principals and a clearly identifiable demonstration while IceCube does not.
responses.response: You are right, and this is why I have moved. Nothing in the first round resolved how a one-name IceCube credit can be defended against the collaboration, the instrument builders and DUMAND, Baikal and AMANDA. I raised that problem myself and then listed the part anyway, and as chair and as someone who works in an adjacent field I should not carry a part that my colleagues cannot check and that I cannot check either. I also agree that your own test, clear attribution, favours B051. Where I stay with you is on the stricter point: your request for an expert statement that the lattice clock is distinct from comb and ion clocks should go into the outside-expert request.

responses.point: Danielsson would support B009 only if expert reports confirm that Halzen's conception and leadership are what the community regards as decisive, and otherwise drop it and fall back to B050 and not widen the credit.
responses.response: I accept that test and I cannot say the evidence for it is in front of us. I read the one-name credit as a conditional, not a settled position, and the conditions are not met, so I no longer put B009 in my preferred configuration. I do not fall back to B050 as my lead, because the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap seems to me a worse attribution problem than the clock one, but I take your point that B050 is the right fallback if B051 fails. I would still cite the 2013 diffuse flux alone if B009 were ever revived, for the reason you gave.

responses.point: Eriksson argues that Kane and Mele supplied the invariant before the HgTe proposal and that Molenkamp's experiment is the decisive test, so a narrow citation on the quantum spin Hall effect and time-reversal-invariant topological insulators can honestly reflect that chain.
responses.response: That is a fair argument and it improves my reading of B050: the citation can follow the Kane-Mele-to-Molenkamp chain without claiming the whole subject. It does not remove my concern that the HgTe route was the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and that the 2016 prize covers adjacent topology, and I rely on you and Mehlig for the condensed-matter judgement. I keep B050 as my first alternative. Your own words that the clocks are a good second choice and that you would not object if the committee preferred them is the closest the table has come to a position that most members can accept.

responses.point: Lindroth locates the distinct step in magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms, argues that waiting for the redefinition of the second is unnecessary, and says she cannot settle the 2001-2003 priority history from memory.
responses.response: I adopt your wording on timing: the clock result stands without a metrology decision, and the citation should say invention and realization of lattice clocks, not the second. On priority, we agree that memory is not enough. I would ask that the outside-expert request ask three plain questions: is the lattice clock distinct from combs and ion clocks, what exactly did Katori propose and demonstrate and when, and what is Ye's credit for, the invention, the accuracy and stability records, or the many-body clock. If the answer is that Ye's credit is refinement, I would want the committee to consider Katori alone and not defend a pair on habit.

uncertainties: Whether outside experts will agree that the lattice clock is distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes and not a continuation of them.
Whether the priority record supports exactly Katori and Ye, and what Ye's credit rests on (invention, accuracy records or the many-body clock); Lemonde and others could be seen as decisive.
Whether a single-part prize is too narrow for the committee; if the committee wants a second part, I have no credit for B009 that I can defend, and B050 depends on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang question.
I have still not verified the current significance of the NGC 1068 and Galactic-plane neutrino results.
statement.conflict_note: No formal conflict for B051. My profile shows no connection to Katori or Ye. I work in PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur, so IceCube (B009) is an adjacent field in which I may be a stronger advocate than a neutral reader, which is one reason I have removed it from my own configuration. I know of no tie to the IceCube team. I rely on colleagues for the atomic-physics and condensed-matter judgements. I note Johansson's disclosed position on B038 and agree he should step back from any decision on it.
